card_summary: The recent announcement about NAB 2026 presentations is a signal that the industry is still grappling with the nuances of live signal transport and latency. As engineers, we know that ST 2110 and NDI have become the de facto standards for real-time transport, but the devil lies in the details – specifically, the need for precise genlock and frame-accuracy to ensure signal integrity. The use of 12G-SDI and JPEG XS for high-bandwidth applications is a step in the right direction, but the industry still needs to address the latency introduced by these technologies. In practice, this means that engineering teams will need to carefully balance the benefits of high-bandwidth transport with the potential latency introduced by these technologies. The trade-off here is between the quality of the signal and the delay introduced by the transport mechanism. For example, using RIST or SRT for low-latency transport may compromise on signal quality, while using ST 2110 with NMOS may introduce unacceptable latency. As engineers, we need to carefully evaluate these trade-offs and make informed decisions about the transport mechanisms we choose for our live signal transport applications.

Why Real-Time Transport Is Forcing Broadcasters to Rethink Signal Integrity

With the increasing adoption of IP-based live signal transport, broadcasters are facing a critical inflection point: ensuring the integrity of their real-time signals. The shift from traditional SDI to IP-based transport has opened up new possibilities for flexible and scalable live production, but it also introduces new challenges related to signal latency, packet loss, and jitter. As a result, broadcasters must reassess their signal transport infrastructure to ensure that it can meet the demands of real-time broadcasting.

What This Development Actually Means

The recent announcement by NUGEN Audio CEO Dr. Paul Tapper to lead a presentation on dialog intelligibility and loudness at NAB 2026 signals a growing focus on the importance of signal quality in live broadcasting. This development is part of a broader trend towards greater emphasis on audio and video quality in live production, driven by the increasing adoption of IP-based transport and the need for more flexible and scalable live production workflows.

This trend is being driven by the growing demand for high-quality live content, particularly in the sports and news markets. Broadcasters are under pressure to deliver high-quality signals with minimal latency, while also ensuring that their infrastructure is scalable and flexible enough to meet the demands of live production.

Why It Matters for Broadcast Operations

The shift towards IP-based live signal transport has significant implications for broadcast operations, particularly in terms of signal integrity and latency. Broadcasters must ensure that their infrastructure can support the demands of real-time broadcasting, including the need for low latency, high-quality signals, and flexible and scalable workflows. This requires a careful assessment of the trade-offs between different technologies and architectures, including the use of ST 2110, NDI, and SRT for IP-based transport, as well as the need for genlock and 12G-SDI for high-quality video signals.

For example, Matrox ConvertIP is a popular choice for IP gateways, while Riedel MediorNet is a leading provider of IP-based signal transport solutions. Avid iNEWS and Vizrt Trio are also key players in the newsroom market, with Pebble Beach Systems and Evertz Mediator-X offering playout solutions that integrate with IP-based transport infrastructure.
